L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), issued by the DGI. Since 1 July 2013, valid RUC numbers have 14 digits, and holders of old 10-digit numbers had to update them at their tax office (DGI provision, 2013). Individuals register with their cédula (residence card for resident foreigners); registration can be started on dgi.gob.ni (search summary).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: Régimen Especial de Estimación Administrativa por Cuota Fija: individuals may opt for a fixed monthly quota if their annual gross income from selling goods and/or providing services does not exceed C$480,000 (2006 reform of Ministerial Agreement 22-2003). Inventory limits and other conditions also apply. Current thresholds may differ, so confirm with the DGI.

sources.title: Reforma al Acuerdo Ministerial 22-2003 — Régimen Especial de Estimación Administrativa para Contribuyentes por Cuota Fija
sources.quote: Posean Ingresos Brutos Anuales por concepto de ventas de bienes y/o prestación de servicios no excedan de los C$ 480,000.00 (cuatrocientos ochenta mil córdobas).

L7_incentives.note: Official text captured is the 2006 reform (Gaceta No. 102); later changes to the thresholds were not checked, and one secondary guide cites C$100,000 a month.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (2) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
